video_title: Enes Kanter on WNBA Controversy, Being Blackballed from the NBA & Death Threats | Curious Mike

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on being blackballed from the NBA for his political activism
quotes.excerpt: they cannot give you the full coverage because you have a higher percentage chance of getting killed.
quotes.quote: I tried to get life insurance around two years ago, and the company said, we cannot give you the full coverage because you have a higher percentage chance of getting killed. If you say another word, you are not going to be able to play basketball ever again in this league. And you are not only going to lose your career, but you are going to lose against about 40 to 50 million dollars. I hung up the phone. I never talked to them again.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his decade-long fight against the Turkish government
quotes.excerpt: the support that I got from Adam Silver, the commissioner, and some of my teammates was amazing.
quotes.quote: For the last 10 years, I talk about the problems that were happening in Turkey. I have been fighting against the Turkish dictatorship my whole life. They put my dad in jail. I haven't seen my family almost 14 years now. They put a bounty on my head and they have been actively trying to kill me now. But the support that I got from Adam Silver, the commissioner, and some of my teammates was amazing. It gave me so much hope to fight for what's right.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on being forced to apologize for his comments on China
quotes.excerpt: the NBA made me put some of the stuff out there that I didn't want to say.
quotes.quote: When I tweeted back in 2019 and said stand with Hong Kong, they made me take my tweet down. They made me apologize. The NBA made me put some of the stuff out there that I didn't want to say. But they said, you don't take your tweet down, you keep talking, which I'm because no other athlete is going to do what you're doing. So at that point, I'm like, I cannot believe it. The NBA has lost 150 million dollars but by one tweet to Daryl Morey.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his close relationship with Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: me and Jaylen Brown, when I was playing for the Celtics, we were sitting next to each other.
quotes.quote: I never actually give any name before, but Jaylen Brown. Me and Jaylen Brown, when I was playing for the Celtics, we were sitting next to each other on a plane. He was the one guy that actually really helped me with many things and I think he is the one person that actually is one of the willing to go out there and speak his mind.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his relationship with Steven Adams
quotes.excerpt: I think other players, Steven Adams. He is doing his PT here in DC.
quotes.quote: I think other players, Steven Adams. He is doing his PT here in DC. So me and him, I see him once a week. He is the type of person that don't really care about what people are saying. I think I publicly say that. That's it.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his conversation with Marcus Smart about his activism
quotes.excerpt: I had this one conversation with Marcus Smart, and he walked in the locker room.
quotes.quote: I had this one conversation with Marcus Smart, and he walked in the locker room. He basically said, dude, what are you doing? We don't know what's going on. Can you please explain it to us? What's happening? What are you fighting for? So me and all the Celtics players, we sit down in the locker room. I explained, I'm like, listen, this has nothing to do with politics. I mean, I think you just need to educate yourself really well first, read a lot.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on why fans dislike Kyle Kuzma
quotes.excerpt: if there is one athlete in America that the sports fans would like to punch in the face.
quotes.quote: If there is one player, if there is one athlete in America that the sports fans would like to punch in the face more than Enes Kanter Freedom, is Kyle Kuzma. I look at his tweets lately. I look at some of his take. I'm like, dude, just you got to educate yourself first. I mean, his takes might be worse than his basketball skills.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on being told he would be out of the league for his activism
quotes.excerpt: you're 29 years old, if you say another word, you're not going to be able to play basketball.
quotes.quote: He said, listen, man, I work for you, I don't work for the NBA. You're 29 years old, if you say another word, you're not going to be able to play basketball ever again in this league. And you're not only going to lose your career, but you're going to lose against about 40 to 50 million dollars. I hung up the phone, I never talked to them again.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on LeBron James' comments about him
quotes.excerpt: LeBron comes out and say, well, if I was Knicks, I would have, you know, draft Dennis Smith.
quotes.quote: We drafted this guy named Frank Ntilikina from France. And obviously he's a rookie and he's just trying to like adjust the big city and big spotlights. And LeBron comes out and say, well, if I was Knicks, I would have, you know, draft Dennis Smith. And the next day I walked in the locker room, I saw his face. I'm like, he was just all down and everything, right, Frank? And I was like, I feel bad for the guy.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on confronting LeBron James after his comments
quotes.excerpt: the next day, LeBron comes and just like pushes him and everything.
quotes.quote: The next day, LeBron comes and just like pushes him and everything. I'm like, listen, dude, like you're LeBron, going like trying to like push a rookie. So anyway, I got in and then me and him got into like a little little chat, I'll say, a little chat.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his WNBA protest
quotes.excerpt: Gabby Williams came out and said, I will welcome a trans athlete in my team or against my team.
quotes.quote: After the game, one of the players, Gabby Williams, came out and said, I will welcome a trans athlete in my team or against my team. And I'm just sitting there, right? I'm like, I cannot believe she said that. So I didn't just, I was just trying to understand it, right? I know that like cancel culture is real and all these players trying to be trying to play the game, I'll say, a little chat.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter Freedom
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his WNBA protest and the league's reaction
quotes.excerpt: I am not suing the WNBA. The reason is I don't want them to lose money.
quotes.quote: I'm not suing the WNBA. The reason is I don't want them to lose money because I want them to be able to keep paying paying these players because they don't really make a lot of money. I'm suing the Chicago Sky and the arena itself because arena partially controlled by the city. So we are suing the city and Chicago Sky. I'm not suing the whole league.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter claims most NBA players oppose the LGBTQ community
quotes.excerpt: probably over 90-95 percent of the players, NBA players in the league, are against the LGBTQ community
quotes.quote: I played 11 years in the NBA. If you ask me, probably over 90-95 percent of the players, NBA players in the league, are against the LGBTQ community. But they will never come out and say it. Why? Because they are scared of the cancel culture. They won't be able to get another contract, they won't be able to get another endorsement deals.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter discusses being blackballed from the NBA for his activism
quotes.excerpt: people think that I'm an enemy, right? People think I'm an extremist, people think I am the psychopath
quotes.quote: People think that I'm an enemy, right? People think I'm an extremist, people think I am the psychopath that's trying to come every sports organization in America. I'm not. I'm not a difficult person to deal with. I either follow your rules or just listen to what I have to say.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter claims he is blacklisted by many governments
quotes.excerpt: my name is on Interpol list. So, in many government sides, I'm an international criminal
quotes.quote: My name is on Interpol list. So, in many government sides, I'm an international criminal. I'm only allowed to travel to 29 countries in the world. Everywhere I go, I have to let FBI know.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his experience being excluded from team travel
quotes.excerpt: I was not even allowed to drive the team bus with the players
quotes.quote: At one point, I was not even allowed to drive the team bus with the players. I used to drive the second bus with the trainers and the media. All the players thought that China or Russia or Iran just going to nuke our team bus, which was not going to happen, but it got to a point it was like so scary. They didn't want me to be in the same bus with me.

quotes.speaker: Enes Kanter
quotes.summary_phrase: Enes Kanter on his NBA legacy beyond statistics
quotes.excerpt: how many lives I have changed, how many hearts I have touched, how many kids I inspired
quotes.quote: When I played 11 years in NBA, I wanted to look back and I'm like, okay, I averaged 10-11 points, 8-9 rebounds, whatever. But the real thing was, how many lives I have changed, how many hearts I have touched, how many kids I inspired. Because once you die, this is what God going to ask you. I gave you all that, what did you do with it?
